mainTopic: How far a זריקה reaches loaves that left the עזרה, and whether the lambs of עצרת can be sprinkled שלא לשמן once their loaves are lost
overview: The amud opens with a משנה from מסכת מעילה. There רבי אליעזר says the זריקה does nothing for sacrificial parts that left the עזרה, while רבי עקיבא says it still takes effect. Building on רבי עקיבא, the גמרא asks about the loaves of עצרת. Since a פיגול זריקה makes loaves that left into פיגול, does a זריקה שלא לשמה also permit them, or does this work only to be strict? רב פפא questions the premise. Maybe everyone agrees that זריקה does nothing for loaves still outside, and the argument is only about loaves brought back in, depending on whether שחיטה makes the loaves holy. The גמרא tries to reject his reading using רב גידל's rule that a פיגול זריקה has no effect on מעילה. But that rule was already refuted, so רב פפא's reading stands. Next, רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא about lambs of עצרת whose loaves were lost after the שחיטה: may their blood be sprinkled שלא לשמן to permit the meat? רבי זירא says no, and narrows his rule twice to answer challenges from the פסח. He then turns aside the challenge from a תודה, since the Torah calls a תודה שלמים. The amud ends as a ברייתא begins about two lambs slaughtered with four loaves, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה in מעילה: רבי אליעזר's view on portions that left before the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about אימורים of קדשים קלים that left the עזרה before the blood was sprinkled. רבי אליעזר says the sprinkling has no effect on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the sacrificial portions of קדשים קלים that went out of the עזרה before the blood was sprinkled. רבי אליעזר says there is no מעילה with them, and no liability for פיגול, נותר or eating them while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source for the idea that, according to רבי עקיבא, the זריקה still affects parts that left the עזרה. This is the background for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים קלים, the אימורים only become fully 'ה׳'s' and subject to מעילה once the blood is sprinkled. רבי אליעזר holds that if they already left the עזרה, the זריקה does nothing to them at all. So none of the usual sacrificial prohibitions apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Offerings of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
Went out of the עזרה, which normally disqualifies them
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the key act of the offering
Being liable for מעילה, the misuse of holy property

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not the main topic. The גמרא only brings it to show that רבי עקיבא holds the זריקה works even on things that left the עזרה. The real question about the loaves comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
The sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity
that went out of the courtyard before the sprinkling of the blood,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
one is not liable for misusing them,
and one is not liable for eating them
due to piggul, notar, or impurity.
phrases.notes: 'Impurity' here means eating holy meat while you yourself are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the premise, stated just before this passage, that רבי עקיבא holds זריקה works on parts that left the עזרה.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי עקיבא, זריקה affects sacrificial parts that left the עזרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת מעילה about אימורי קדשים קלים that left before זריקה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's view: the sprinkling still takes effect
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. He holds there is מעילה, and there is liability for פיגול, נותר and טמא, even though the portions left before the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: there is מעילה with them, and one is liable for them due to פיגול, נותר and eating while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי עקיבא's opposing view: the זריקה does take effect on portions that already left the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, leaving the עזרה does not stop the זריקה from 'reaching' the portions. They become fully subject to all the laws of holy items. This is the principle the גמרא will now test with the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the intent to eat or offer it at the wrong time; eating it brings כרת
Sacrificial meat left past its allowed eating time
Ritually impure; here it refers to eating holy food while impure

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא holds that the זריקה still affects sacrificial items even after they left the עזרה. רבי אליעזר holds that it does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
one is liable for misusing them,
and one is liable for eating them
due to piggul, notar, or impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, זריקה takes effect on אימורים that left the עזרה, so מעילה, פיגול, נותר and טמא all apply.

steps.title: The dilemma: if a פיגול sprinkling affects the loaves, does a שלא לשמה sprinkling permit them?
steps.stepSummary: Within רבי עקיבא's view, the גמרא asks about the loaves. A פיגול זריקה makes them פיגול even after they left. So does a זריקה שלא לשמה also permit them to be eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since a פיגול sprinkling fixes the loaves as פיגול even when they went out, just like the meat, should we say that a sprinkling שלא לשמה also permits the loaves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its original question about the lambs of עצרת whose blood was sprinkled שלא לשמה. It now lays out the first side of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already see that the זריקה has power over loaves that left the עזרה, because a פיגול sprinkling makes them פיגול. So it seems logical that the same זריקה, done שלא לשמה, should work on them in the lenient direction too. Then they would be permitted, just like the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Done with intent for a different offering than the one it really is
Fixed or established the loaves in a status
Permits (Aramaic)
Here, the שתי הלחם brought with the lambs on עצרת

phrases.english: What is the law?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the question about the lambs of עצרת that were slaughtered for their own sake but whose blood was sprinkled for another sake.

phrases.english: Since a piggul sprinkling fixes the bread as piggul
even when the bread went out, just like the meat,
a sprinkling not for its own sake
also permits the bread,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? מִדִּזְרִיקַת פִּיגּוּל קָבְעָה לְלֶחֶם בְּפִיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי עקיבא's principle from the משנה to the case of the loaves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי עקיבא, does a זריקה שלא לשמה permit the loaves the way it permits the meat?

steps.title: Second side: maybe we apply it only to be strict, not to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the doubt: perhaps the power of זריקה over loaves that left applies only for stringency, such as making them פיגול. It would not apply for leniency, such as permitting them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps we say this only to be strict, but to be lenient we do not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second possibility, which completes the two sides of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There may be a difference between strictness and leniency. Letting the זריקה make loaves that left into פיגול is a חומרא. Letting it permit them would be a קולא, and perhaps we do not extend the rule that far. The גמרא does not decide this. Instead, רב פפא next questions whether the premise is even correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; it introduces the second side of a doubt
In the strict direction
In the lenient direction
We say, meaning we apply this rule

steps.whatToRemember: The doubt is this: does the זריקה's power over loaves that left the עזרה work both ways, or only to make things stricter?

phrases.english: Or perhaps we say this only to be stringent,
but to be lenient we do not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the doubt raised in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the power of זריקה over items that left the עזרה applies only לחומרא, or לקולא as well.

steps.title: רב פפא questions the assumed case of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks how we know that רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about loaves that are still outside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: How do we know they argue in a case where the loaves are outside?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the starting assumption of the whole discussion. He asks how we know the argument is about loaves that are still outside. This line sets up his own different reading, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 4 built a question on the idea that, according to רבי עקיבא, זריקה works even on loaves that are outside. If the argument is not about loaves outside at all, that question loses its footing. רב פפא is attacking the foundation, not the details.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it. This introduces a strong challenge to the line of reasoning.
Outside, here meaning outside the עזרה.
They disagree.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to this:
And from where do we know that they disagree when the loaves are outside?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא from the משנה in Step 1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption that the case in Steps 3 and 4 depends on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the מחלוקת is about loaves that are outside the עזרה at the time of זריקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing forces us to read the argument as being about loaves outside. Another case could be meant.

steps.title: רב פפא's alternative reading of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that everyone agrees זריקה does nothing for loaves still outside. The argument is only about loaves that left and were brought back in, and it depends on whether שחיטה makes the loaves holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps, when the loaves are still outside, everyone agrees that זריקה does nothing for them. They argue only when the loaves were brought back in. רבי אליעזר holds like רבי, who says שחיטה makes the loaves holy, so they already became פסול by leaving. רבי עקיבא holds like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says שחיטה does not make them holy, so leaving does not make them פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא lays out his own version of the argument. Both sides agree about loaves that are still outside. They argue only about loaves that left and came back, and each side follows a different view on what שחיטה does to the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שחיטה already makes the loaves holy, as רבי says, then leaving the עזרה made them פסול. Bringing them back does not help, so זריקה cannot affect them, which matches רבי אליעזר. If שחיטה does not make them holy, as רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, leaving did them no harm, so זריקה works on them once they are back inside, which matches רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood does not take effect on something that has left the עזרה.
He then brought them back in.
The slaughter of the animals makes the loaves holy.
Something holy that left its proper area, which makes it פסול.
They become פסול (disqualified).

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אליעזר, who argues with רבי עקיבא in the משנה, with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, whose view רבי עקיבא is said to follow here. They are two different people.

phrases.english: Perhaps, where the loaves are still outside,
everyone agrees
that sprinkling does not take effect on what has left,
and they disagree where he then brought them back in,
for Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabbi,
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: who said: the slaughter makes them holy,
and so they became disqualified by leaving.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
who said: the slaughter does not make them holy,
and so they do not become disqualified by leaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the alternative reading that the challenge in Step 5 hinted at.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי עקיבא holds זריקה works on loaves that are still outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different case, loaves brought back in, explains both opinions just as well. It also ties the argument to whether שחיטה makes the loaves holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this reading holds, the question in Steps 3 and 4 falls apart, because no one holds that זריקה works on loaves that are still outside.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's words fit only if slaughter makes the loaves holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's reading. רבי עקיבא's own words fit well if he holds like רבי, that שחיטה makes the loaves holy and זריקה then fixes them as פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? It makes sense if רבי עקיבא holds like רבי, who says שחיטה makes the loaves holy. That is why רבי עקיבא says the loaves become holy through the שחיטה, and then the זריקה comes and fixes them as פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to push back against רב פפא. It shows that רבי עקיבא's ruling of פיגול fits well with the view that שחיטה makes the loaves holy. This sets up the problem with רב פפא's version, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's ruling of liability for פיגול is explained this way: the loaves became holy at the שחיטה, and the זריקה then fixed them as פיגול. That only works if he holds like רבי. But רב פפא said רבי עקיבא holds like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says שחיטה does not make the loaves holy, so under his reading it is hard to see how רבי עקיבא's ruling of פיגול could apply.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? A rejection meaning the suggestion does not fit.
Granted, or it makes sense if. This sets up a contrast with what does not make sense.
Fixes them as פיגול, locking in the פיגול status.

phrases.english: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כְּרַבִּי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: It makes sense if you say Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi,
who said: the slaughter makes them holy,
that is why Rabbi Akiva says
that they become holy through the slaughter,
and the sprinkling comes and fixes them as piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's reading in Step 6 by checking it against רבי עקיבא's own words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב פפא's claim that רבי עקיבא holds like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא speaks of the loaves becoming holy through שחיטה. That fits only the view of רבי, not the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: If רבי עקיבא held like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, a פיגול זריקה could not make the loaves holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting רב פפא. If רבי עקיבא held that שחיטה does not make the loaves holy, a זריקה done with פיגול intent would not make them holy either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say רבי עקיבא holds like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who said that slaughter does not make the loaves holy, does a פיגול sprinkling make them holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the other possibility for רבי עקיבא, the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. It asks a pointed question that shows this view cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the loaves become holy only through the זריקה. Only loaves that are already holy can become פיגול. So the whole question is whether a זריקה done with פיגול intent is strong enough to make them holy. The expected answer is no.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter of the animal (the same as שחיטה)
Makes holy, gives the loaves קדושה
Sprinkling the blood with an intent that makes the offering פיגול
He holds (this opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון with רבי אליעזר from the משנה. These are two different תנאים.

phrases.english: But if you say

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that he holds like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
who said: slaughter does not make the loaves holy,
does a פיגול sprinkling make them holy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes the rejection begun in Step 7. Step 7 showed רבי עקיבא fits with רבי's view, and this step shows he cannot fit with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possibility that רבי עקיבא, under רב פפא's reading, holds like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that view only the זריקה makes the loaves holy. A פיגול זריקה is not strong enough to do that, so the loaves could never become פיגול.

steps.title: רב: a פיגול זריקה neither brings items into מעילה nor takes them out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that a פיגול זריקה has no power to make things holy. It cites רב גידל in the name of רב, who said it does not affect מעילה in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב גידל say in the name of רב: a פיגול sprinkling does not bring items into מעילה, and it does not take items out of מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its question from Step 8. It shows that a פיגול זריקה does not count as a real זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid זריקה changes the status of the offering's parts with regard to מעילה. רב says a פיגול זריקה changes nothing, so it acts as if no זריקה happened at all. If it cannot change the offering itself, it surely cannot make the loaves holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against using הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit
Brings into (a status)
Takes out of (a status)
But didn't he say (introduces a source that proves the point)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that a פיגול זריקה acts as if no זריקה happened. It can make the offering פיגול, but it cannot do the positive work of a real זריקה.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Giddel say that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: זְרִיקַת פִּיגּוּל אֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה לִידֵי מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: a פיגול sprinkling does not bring items into מעילה,
and it does not take items out of מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the source behind Step 8's rhetorical question.
steps.raayaObject: That a פיגול זריקה cannot make the loaves holy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב גידל in the name of רב: a פיגול זריקה does not bring items into מעילה and does not take them out of it.

steps.title: Explaining the two halves of רב's rule
steps.stepSummary: "Does not bring into מעילה" refers to the אימורים of קדשים קלים. "Does not take out of מעילה" refers to the meat of קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "It does not bring into מעילה" refers to the parts burned on the altar from offerings of lesser holiness. "It does not take out of מעילה" refers to the meat of offerings of the highest holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly which cases each half of רב's rule is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים קלים, a valid זריקה makes the altar parts (אימורים) subject to מעילה, but a פיגול זריקה does not. With קדשי קדשים, a valid זריקה releases the meat from מעילה so the כהנים may eat it, but after a פיגול זריקה the meat stays under מעילה. In both cases the פיגול זריקה acts as if nothing happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness, such as a חטאת or an אשם
The meat of the offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב גידל in the name of רב, a פיגול זריקה does not work like a real זריקה: it neither creates מעילה nor removes it. The next step shows this statement was refuted, so it cannot be used against רב פפא.

phrases.english: "It does not bring into מעילה" —
refers to the altar parts of offerings of lesser holiness.
phrases.notes: After a valid זריקה these parts would become subject to מעילה. A פיגול זריקה does not make that happen.

phrases.english: And "it does not take out of מעילה" —
refers to the meat of offerings of the highest holiness.
phrases.notes: A valid זריקה would free this meat for the כהנים to eat. After a פיגול זריקה it stays forbidden under מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינָהּ מְבִיאָה לִידֵי מְעִילָה בְּאֵימוּרֵי קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defines the cases that each half of רב's rule from Step 9 refers to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פיגול זריקה does not make the אימורים of קדשים קלים subject to מעילה, and it does not release the meat of קדשי קדשים from מעילה.

steps.title: The proof from רב גידל does not stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רב גידל because his statement was already refuted elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't the statement that רב גידל said in the name of רב refuted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof it just brought from רב גידל. That statement was already refuted, so we cannot build on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא used רב גידל to show that a פיגול זריקה cannot make things holy. Since his statement was refuted, it cannot serve as proof. So the objection from steps 7–8 falls away, and רב פפא's reading of the מחלוקת (step 6) stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Was refuted; a statement that was disproven and can no longer be relied on

phrases.english: Wasn't it refuted
that which רב גידל said in the name of רב?
phrases.notes: This is the statement quoted in step 9 about מעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִיתּוֹתַב דְּרַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the proof brought in steps 9-10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רב גידל's statement about מעילה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source statement was already refuted, so it has no authority as proof.

steps.title: Sheep slaughtered for their sake, then the loaves were lost
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the blood may be sprinkled not for its sake so the meat can be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: The sheep of שבועות were slaughtered for their own sake, and then the loaves were lost. May the כהן sprinkle their blood שלא לשמן, so the meat can be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי ירמיה asks about the two sheep of שבועות whose loaves got lost after the sheep were slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheep and the loaves go together, so without the loaves, sprinkling the blood לשמן would not permit the meat. רבי ירמיה wants to know if sprinkling the blood שלא לשמן, as a regular offering, gets around the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The two sheep offered on שבועות together with the two loaves
For their own sake (as the offering they are) / not for their own sake (as a different offering)
The two loaves of שבועות that go with the sheep

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא:
The sheep of שבועות that one slaughtered for their own sake,
and the loaves were lost –
what is the law: may he sprinkle their blood not for their own sake
to permit the meat to be eaten?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the כבשי עצרת and their loaves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether sprinkling the blood שלא לשמן can permit the meat once the loaves are lost.

steps.title: Nothing is unfit for its sake yet fit not for its sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that it makes no sense for an offering to be unfit לשמו but fit שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is there anything that is not fit for its own sake, yet is fit not for its own sake?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers no. Sprinkling שלא לשמן cannot help where sprinkling לשמן does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: doing an offering for its real purpose is the best way. If the best way does not work, a 'wrong' way should not work better.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, valid as an offering

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּשֵׁר לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: Do you have anything that is not fit for its own sake,
and is fit not for its own sake?!

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּשֵׁר לִשְׁמוֹ וְכָשֵׁר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; an offering unfit לשמו cannot become fit שלא לשמו.

steps.title: Challenge from a פסח before midday
steps.stepSummary: A פסח slaughtered before חצות is unfit as a פסח but fit as a different offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there no such thing? There is the פסח before midday: it is not fit for its own sake, yet it is fit not for its own sake!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back with a case that seems to break רבי זירא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before חצות on the fourteenth of ניסן, it is too early to bring a פסח, so slaughtering it as a פסח does not work. Yet slaughtering it as a שלמים does work, so here is something unfit לשמו but fit שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: A Pesach offering before midday of the fourteenth of ניסן, before its proper time
Peace offering; the other offering the פסח can be brought as before its time

phrases.english: And is there not?!
But there is the פסח before midday,
which is not fit for its own sake,
and is fit not for its own sake!
phrases.notes: He means slaughtering it as a שלמים, which is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that nothing is unfit לשמו yet fit שלא לשמו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח before חצות is a clear example: invalid as a פסח, valid as a שלמים.

steps.title: Once fit, then pushed off
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא narrows his rule to an offering that was fit לשמו and then got pushed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I am saying: Is there anything that was fit for its own sake, and was then pushed off from its own sake, so it is not fit for its own sake, yet it is fit not for its own sake?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains what he really meant, so the פסח case no longer contradicts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח before חצות was never fit as a פסח yet. These sheep were fit לשמן when slaughtered, and only lost that when the loaves were lost. רבי זירא says something that was once fit and then pushed off does not become fit שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: Was fit, was ready to be offered
Was pushed off, lost its fitness

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's rule: an offering that was once fit לשמו and then was pushed off cannot be saved by doing it שלא לשמו. A פסח before חצות is different because it was never fit as a פסח.

phrases.english: This is what I am saying:
Do you have anything that was fit for its own sake,
and was pushed off from its own sake,
and is not fit for its own sake,
and yet is fit not for its own sake?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from פסח by narrowing the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying and narrowing the original rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא's rule seemed to cover any offering unfit לשמו, so the פסח before חצות contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only covers an offering that was once fit לשמו and then pushed off; the פסח before חצות was never fit, so it is a different case.

steps.title: A פסח after its time
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges the narrowed rule from a פסח offered after its time, during the rest of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really no such case? What about a פסח after its time, during the rest of the year, before midday!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא's narrowed rule from step 15. He brings a פסח that was fit in its own time and was later pushed off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 רבי זירא said his rule covers only an offering that was fit לשמו and then got pushed off. A פסח fits that description: it was fit as a פסח in its time. After its time it can no longer be brought as a פסח, yet it can be brought as a different offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A Passover offering after its proper time has passed
The rest of the days of the year
Midday

phrases.english: And is there not?
But there is the Passover offering after its time,
during the rest of the days of the year, before midday!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the narrowed rule given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that an offering which was fit לשמו and then pushed off cannot become fit שלא לשמו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח was fit לשמו in its time. After its time it is pushed off as a פסח, but it is still fit as another offering.

steps.title: רבי זירא adds: already slaughtered for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא narrows his rule again: he means an offering that was slaughtered לשמו while fit, and only after that was pushed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I meant: Do you have anything that was fit for its own sake, was slaughtered for its own sake, then was pushed off from its own sake, and is not fit for its own sake but is fit not for its own sake?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers by explaining what he really meant. He adds one more condition: the offering was actually slaughtered לשמו before it got pushed off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח after its time was never slaughtered as a פסח; it was pushed off before slaughtering. The case under discussion is the two lambs of שבועות, which were slaughtered לשמו and then lost their loaves. רבי זירא says nothing like that ever switches to being fit שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I meant (clarifying one's own earlier statement)
Was fit to be offered for its own sake
Was slaughtered for its own sake

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rounds. In step 15 the condition was 'fit and then pushed off.' Here the new condition is that it was already slaughtered לשמו before being pushed off.

phrases.english: This is what I am saying:
Do you have anything that was fit for its own sake,
and was slaughtered for its own sake, and was pushed off from its own sake,
and it is not fit for its own sake,
and it is fit not for its own sake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 16 by tightening the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to cover any offering that was fit לשמו and later pushed off, which would include a פסח after its time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only an offering that was actually slaughtered לשמו and pushed off afterward. A פסח after its time does not fit this description.

steps.title: The תודה whose loaves broke
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges again from a תודה whose loaves became unfit after it was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there no such case? What about the תודה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges the newest version of the rule. He points to a תודה that fits every one of רבי זירא's conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As taught earlier (46a), if a תודה is slaughtered and then its loaves break, its blood is sprinkled as a שלמים so the meat can be eaten. So it was slaughtered לשמו, then pushed off, and is now fit only שלא לשמו. That seems to be exactly what רבי זירא said never happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering, which is brought together with loaves

phrases.english: And is there not?! But there is the thanks offering!
phrases.notes: He means a תודה whose loaves broke after it was slaughtered, as taught earlier on 46a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the further-narrowed rule from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule as narrowed in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תודה slaughtered לשמו whose loaves later broke can't be completed as a תודה, yet its blood is sprinkled as a שלמים. This is a case that meets all the conditions.

steps.title: A תודה is called שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that a תודה is different, because the Torah calls it שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תודה is different, because the Merciful One calls it 'שלמים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends his rule by showing the תודה is a special case. It doesn't really count as switching to a different offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah itself calls a תודה 'שלמים' (ויקרא 7:13), and a שלמים is brought without loaves. So a תודה is not truly ruined when its loaves are lost; it can still go forward as a שלמים. That makes it different from the lambs of שבועות, which are bound to their loaves, and רבי זירא's rule still stands for them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (a special case)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's rule: an offering slaughtered לשמו and then pushed off cannot become fit שלא לשמו. The תודה is no exception, because the Torah calls it שלמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי זירא's rule standing, so blood of the שבועות lambs whose loaves were lost cannot be sprinkled שלא לשמו to allow the meat.

phrases.english: The thanks offering is different,
as the Merciful One called it a 'peace offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the תודה in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A תודה offered as a שלמים looked like an offering pushed off from its own sake and made fit for a different sake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah calls a תודה 'שלמים', and a שלמים comes without loaves. So a תודה is not truly pushed off when its loaves are lost, unlike the lambs of שבועות, and רבי זירא's rule remains intact.

steps.title: Two sheep slaughtered with four loaves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the two sheep were slaughtered with four loaves, two loaves are taken out and waved with the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone slaughtered two sheep together with four loaves, he takes two of the loaves and waves them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the two sheep and their loaves, where there were four loaves instead of two. This line sets up the case, and the ברייתא continues next with what happens to the other two loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sheep are supposed to come with only two loaves, but here four loaves were there when the sheep were slaughtered. The first ruling is simple: pull out two of them and do the waving with those two. The open question, which the ברייתא answers next, is what status the extra two loaves have.

keyTerms.meaning: The two sheep that are brought together with the loaves
Loaves
He draws out, takes out
He waves them (does the תְּנוּפָה, the waving of the offering)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׂים עַל אַרְבַּע חַלּוֹת –
phrases.english: If one slaughtered two sheep on four loaves,
phrases.notes: "On" means together with. Normally the two sheep come with only two loaves, so there are two too many here.

phrases.english: he draws two of them and waves them,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׂים עַל אַרְבַּע חַלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי זירא and רבי ירמיה exchange ends with the answer about תודה, the גמרא opens a new ברייתא about the two sheep and their loaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the two sheep were slaughtered with four loaves, two of the loaves are taken out and waved with the sheep. The ruling for the remaining two loaves comes next.
